quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care between 2008 and 2019.

rationale: Source is described with a time frame (2008-2019) and a platform type (hospital database), but the database is not named, no snapshot date is given and no explicit route from a task to its source record is stated. Release IDs and provenance notes are mentioned only generally.

quotes.text: All patient records originate from a de-identified hospital database collected during routine care
released under a credentialed-access data use agreement
review board determined that the study qualified for a waiver of consent

rationale: Origin, collection setting, terms (credentialed-access DUA) and consent status (waiver) are all stated. Appendix A also says the data terms are separate from the MIT code licence. Note: the paper elsewhere calls the cases MedQA-derived, which sits oddly with a hospital-database origin.

searched: S1 (no comparison of patient features with a target population or descriptive demographics), S2 and S3 (no chunks), S4 (agent_eval/notes.py comment describes a representativeness comparison, but code comments never count as reporting under G1a), S5 (no chunks).

quotes.text: Non-dangerous diagnosis | 0.550 | 0.680 | +0.130 | McNemar, p=0.0351

rationale: An unsafe-output measure is reported (non-dangerous diagnosis rate, plus unsafe or unsupported element indicators in the manager score). No test is framed as a bias test; the sex/race subgroup reporting is slice reporting, not a dedicated bias test, so the score is 1.

quotes.text: Released tasks include a canary string.
A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces.

rationale: Developer-side controls are present (canary string, private held-out split, web access blocked). No measured overlap or contamination check is reported, so 2 is not reached.

quotes.text: the answer labels are stored in a separate evaluation service that has no network path from the agent sandbox

rationale: Isolation is stated with named mechanisms: separate evaluation service with no network path from the agent sandbox, and labels not published in the repository.

quotes.text: the database snapshot, the software image and the simulated-patient language model are all pinned to fixed versions

rationale: Data, software image and simulator model are stated as pinned, with no external service called at evaluation time other than the model under test. The manager/judge model is not named separately, but the no-external-call statement covers it.

quotes.text: we ran a scripted reference solution for each task through the grader; all 120 reference solutions were graded correct

rationale: A scripted reference solution was run through the grader for each task and the result is reported. The 120-task count differs from the 700 episodes elsewhere in the paper; noted only.

quotes.text: Grading validates both intended state modifications and preservation of unrelated records.

rationale: Tasks are stated to change state, so NA does not apply. The grader is stated to check both changed and unchanged (unrelated) records, and unintended changes are scored as failures.

quotes.text: Random-action agents achieve 3.1% success across tasks.
Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: Empirical random-action and no-action rates are reported. The two random-agent figures differ (3.1% versus 2.5%); noted as an internal inconsistency, but both are low empirical rates.

quotes.text: Across all 120 tasks, an agent with no actions scores 0.0%, while a random-action agent achieves 2.5%.

rationale: Do-nothing (0.0%) and random-action (2.5%) agent scores are reported across all 120 tasks. A different random-agent figure (3.1%) appears elsewhere in S1.

quotes.text: We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: Benchmark's own validation with per-class error rates is reported. Appendix E adds a single-physician audit of 100 outputs with agreement and kappa figures.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.
The main text describes the policy of executing each task three times.

rationale: Temperature 0, a fixed seed and a repeated-run policy are stated in S1. The run count conflicts with Appendix Z, which states eight runs per task; noted.

quotes.text: test the difference between the two best models with a paired permutation test (p = 0.02)

rationale: Bootstrap CIs on all model scores and a paired permutation test for the headline comparison of the two best models are reported.

quotes.text: Every run applies temperature 0 with a fixed seed.
we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs

rationale: Runs per task are given (three in the main text, eight in Appendix Z, which conflict) and a seed and temperature 0 are stated. Independence of runs is not stated.

quotes.text: 95% confidence intervals computed by bootstrapping over tasks, so the resampling unit is the task
where several tasks share a patient, we resample patients instead to account for clustering

rationale: 95% bootstrap CIs, the resampling unit (task) and clustering of tasks within patients are all stated. Table 9 also reports CIs on headline scores.

quotes.text: the agreement of the final environment state across the eight runs
we ran each task eight times and report pass^8, the fraction of tasks solved in all eight runs

rationale: A pass^k all-runs metric and final-state agreement across reruns are reported with run count eight. No action-sequence agreement is stated, and the packet shows no numeric values for these metrics.

quotes.text: Models were queried through their APIs using the snapshot identifiers gpt-4o-2024-08-06 and claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022, with temperature 0 and a maximum of 2,048 output tokens
all reported numbers correspond to harness release v1.2.0

rationale: Provider snapshot IDs, decoding parameters and a harness release matching the reported numbers are stated. Caveat: the experiment tables name different models (Qwen, GLM, Kimi) without versions, which does not match the snapshot IDs given.

quotes.text: invalid-test rates come from test-return status

rationale: The benchmark uses a text-command action protocol (ASK, REQUEST_TEST, CALL_MDT, FINALIZE), so NA does not apply. Only partial return semantics are documented (returned-result status, invalid, unavailable and unparseable tests). No per-tool schema is shown and read versus write side effects are not documented in S1-S3; S5 has no chunks, so reach cannot be told.

quotes.text: MedEvoEval is a simulation-based evaluation framework for research use.

rationale: Simulated components (patient simulator, exam service, simulated cases) are disclosed in S1. No tests of tool conformance are reported (only schema and package validation), and S5 has no chunks, so reach to the agent cannot be shown.

quotes.text: Any unintended changes are caught and scored as failures.

rationale: S1 implies state changes are graded, with unintended changes scored as failures, so NA does not apply and element (iii) is partly shown. S1-S3 do not list which actions write or whether writes are sandboxed. The S4 comment in notes.py lists write actions and sandboxing but code comments do not count, and no S5 chunk is present.

quotes.text: The grader takes the final environment state as its input.
We validated the grader on 150 injected correct and incorrect outcomes, finding a false-accept rate of 1% and a false-reject rate of 2%.

rationale: Grader input is stated as final environment state, and validation on injected correct and incorrect outcomes reports per-class error rates. No rationale for a non-state grader is given, but none is required if the input is end state.

quotes.text: Web access is blocked during runs; retrieval is confined to the task environment, preventing answer leakage through search.
A private held-out test split with concealed labels is excluded from all public surfaces.
Released tasks include a canary string.

rationale: Leakage controls (web blocked, confined retrieval), a private split with labels absent from all public surfaces, and a canary string are all stated.

quotes.text: We report accuracy per task family (diagnosis, ordering and documentation tasks) and per patient subgroup by sex and race
each table lists the number of cases in every slice

rationale: Per-task-family and per-subgroup (sex, race) reporting with slice sizes is stated. The tables shown in the packet do not display such slices, so the claim rests on this sentence.

quotes.text: The patient records are real de-identified records from a hospital database.
requiring credentialed access and de-identification by the safe harbour method
the data are released under terms separate from the MIT code licence

rationale: Records are stated as real de-identified, governance (DUA, credentialed access, safe harbour de-identification, waiver) is stated, and data terms are stated as separate from the MIT code licence.
